newsitem.title: KUWAIT: Kuwait tp seek higher OPEC quota says minister.
newsitem.headline: Kuwait tp seek higher OPEC quota says minister.

text.p: Kuwait will demand a higher oil quota at OPEC's November ministerial meeting, newly-appointed Oil Minister Isa al-Mazeedi said in remarks published on Sunday.
The minister said "he will abide by (Kuwait's) demand for a higher quota at the next OPEC meeting in November," al-Qabas newspaper quoted him as telling the daily.
Kuwait, which has an OPEC quota of two million barrels per day (bpd), had said in the past it would demand a rise in its quota if the overall OPEC ceiling is increased.
OPEC, including linchpin Saudi Arabia, has no plans to increase crude quotas when OPEC ministers next meet in November, a Gulf source told Reuters earlier this month.
Oil prices have this month shot to their highest level since the 1991 Gulf War because of low petroleum inventories ahead of the northern hemisphere's winter and Middle East tension.
Analysts said it would be unlikely for OPEC ministers in November to open a debate about quotas when market conditions were so favourable for the oil group.
Mazeedi, appointed in a new 14-man cabinet on Tuesday, was not immediately available for comment on the Qabas report.

Mazeedi "said that the country's declared oil policy will continue as it is with no change, stressing his keeness on safeguarding Kuwait's position in the oil market and getting what it deserves," Qabas added.
